statement: A deadline stays in the unit the contract compares: it is a J height in the hold and the second `terms.secondsOf` gives it in the proof body, and it is never replaced by a stored height. A node reads it against the second of the J block at its view, the header of the same block as the height (never the tip's, never a wall clock or an offset), which travels with the height from the J loop to the Entity (`j_height.seconds`, a field of the WAL row, so a replay has it). blocksLeft(d) = floor((secondsOf(d) - headSeconds) / slot) - missed, and a deadline is read as e(d) = view + min(d - view, blocksLeft(d)): it can shorten, never lengthen. A hub forwards a lock held until d_in as one held until d_out only if e(d_out) is above the view and every claim it may have to land fits between the two deadlines, measured between them and not from now (the payee's reveal may land at d_out itself): min(d_in - d_out, floor((secondsOf(d_in) - secondsOf(d_out)) / slot) - missed) is at least reaction + 1 (R-LAG-ONE). Missed slots cancel between two effective deadlines but not in the seconds window itself, so `missed` stays in the gap. Whenever the gap holds at the view, the two effective deadlines are at least reaction + 1 apart, whether one, both or neither is capped by blocksLeft (a property over random heads). A hub that does not know the second of its view forwards nothing. `slot` and `missed` are in the clock (`ClockParams.pace`, from the chain's manifest or config, no literal), and a node that may hold value does not start without them. There is no deadline-in-seconds knob: each deadline comes from its own lock. Owed: the Arrival and Quint models of the gate; the second of the view block at a boot on a quiet chain is learned with the first height past the view (until then nothing is forwarded).
source: coordinator ruling 10-03 03:32 and 03:50 (reserve bound, hub slack gate); builder; R-DEADLINE-TIMESTAMP; consolidation-plan.md D9
